_: Inhabitants put down by hand, beside the ones a location's own file spawns (its mobs node). Read by server/world.py (placements) and stood in the room by server/rooms.py (Room), after the file's own and under the same kind of entity id, so the client builds them from the same lch;newUser and userInfo_* frames: a Commoner is talked to, a Trader trades, a hostile creature fights, dies and comes back on its cell. Keyed by location id (open desert's is its packed map cell, world.pack); each row is {type: the creature's type id in mobs.xml, cell: [x, y] of the location's own grid, escort: true for a boss's escort, which once killed comes back with the boss's next arrival rather than on the respawn timer (a hostile creature in a location whose file has a boss), patrol: the camp whose patrol the row is, on an open-desert cell next to it (data/build_camp_patrols.py writes every such row and rewrites them whole), why: RECOVERED or DESIGNED and the evidence}. The server checks every row before its first socket (rooms.check_placements) and does not start on one that cannot stand: a type the client has no record or name of, a loot box or heap of ore (role object), a hostile creature in a location at peace, a cell off the grid, on an obstacle, on an exit or on somebody else's spawn. LAVA_PLACEMENTS replaces the table, for a suite that needs one of its own (server/test_valley_world.py).
